items.title: 1- Opening up the DNA double helix

source_refs.note: 1- Opening up the DNA double helix: a main subheading of 19.3.3 Mechanism of DNA Replication, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 126-126.

blocks.text: The replication of DNA begins at one or more sites on DNA molecule where there is a specific sequence of nucleotides called a replication origin site. In prokaryotes, there is only one replication origin site. But in eukaryotes, there are many replication origin sites along the length of DNA.

items: Initiator protein binds to the replication origin site and initiates the process.

At the origin site, the “unwinding” enzymes called helicases break the hydrogen bonds between the nucleotide-pairs (base-pairs) of two strands. The stands separate a little and make two Y-shaped structures called replication forks (collectively called a replication bubble).
Due to unwinding of the DNA helix, supercoils are produced ahead of the replication fork.
The enzyme gyrase (or topoisomerase) attaches ahead of the replication fork. It prevents supercoiling again.
Single-strand binding proteins bind to single strands and prevent them from re-joining and rewinding.
The two replication forks move away from each other so that replication can occur at both forks. Both single strands act as templates for the next steps.
